speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. Please describe your wrist pain, fever, and skin lesions in detail, including when they started and if they are spreading.

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient presents with a 3-day history of pain in his left wrist, which worsened this morning accompanied by chills and malaise. He recounts having a self-resolving left knee pain the previous week. Reports recent return from a camping trip in Minnesota. Sexually active with one female partner. No history of trauma to the wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Lyme disease (Borrelia burgdorferi) presenting with early disseminated symptoms (Lyme arthritis, fever, and possible cutaneous manifestations). Given the patient's camping history in Minnesota, recent self-resolving knee pain (suggesting prior dissemination to the joints), and current wrist pain with systemic symptoms, I suspect a tick-borne infection. The "skin lesions" mentioned may represent erythema migrans or secondary rashes. I recommend requesting images of the wrist and skin to confirm the presence of annular erythema or other characteristic rash patterns. REQUEST IMAGES: Wrist and skin lesions.
